name: Petar Hektorović
bio: Petar Hektorović (1487–1572) was a Croatian poet of the Renaissance, born in Stari Grad on the island of Hvar into a family of the local nobility. He wrote in the Chakavian speech of his island and corresponded with scholars of the Dalmatian coast.

His best-known work is Ribanje i ribarsko prigovaranje (Fishing and Fishermen's Conversations), printed in Venice in 1568, an account of a three-day voyage in verse. He also built the fortified house Tvrdalj at Stari Grad, where he lived and where the voyage begins.
